scope: Model the named Gothic residence with its entrance tower, brick/stone facade and conservatory. It is a separate building from Kensington Palace.

sources.publisher: Survey of London, vol37 Northern Kensington, edited F.H.W.Sheppard,1973
facts: Buff brick and Bath stone; two principal storeys above basement, with a taller central entrance tower.
Central oriel and quatrefoil parapet; rectangular sash openings, diagonal corner buttresses and an open Gothic roof parapet.
The1924Parvin alterations removed the bell turret, added front/back steps and a timber porch, and changed conservatory glazing and its roof from sloping to flat.
sources.inspection: Primary full HTML retrieved and relevant house section read. Modern1973photographs/plates are excluded as architectural imagery; no such image fetched.

sources.publisher: Historic England, National Heritage List for England
facts: Symmetrical4:3:4composition, central tower/oriel, sash windows, open Gothic tracery parapet, diagonal corner buttresses and four-centred entrance with Gothic canopy.
sources.inspection: Primary statutory descriptive text only; contributed photographs/maps not adopted.

facts: Architect’s illustrated account includes the complete exterior, ground plan and conservatory.
Historical conservatory dimension40×21feet; current model follows the present mapped envelope rather than forcing historic room dimensions onto modern fabric.
sources.inspection: Two exact native published illustrations inspected; other book images/interiors not adopted.

limits: Original illustrated turret/roof and historic plans are not a certification of unchanged current architecture. Later alterations are independently described.
Main-roof levels/drainage, exact conservatory glazing, small door/porch profiles and hidden elevations remain medium-fi interpretations.
No exact1924interior reconstruction, security fixtures, garden, flag or street furniture.
